punchline: In 1996 more than a hundred cities asked for Southwest Airlines, and it chose to open just four.
thirty_sec: Paul Jarvis has a great example in Company of One. In 1996 more than a hundred cities wanted Southwest Airlines at their airports. Southwest added four. He says that restraint helped it stay profitable while most airlines were losing money. His point is that goals need a ceiling as well as a floor. Before growing, ask whether you need it, and whether you could do it with what you already have.
